passage:
There was one lunch table in the cafeteria where students did not talk much. It was not a punishment table. It was called the Quiet Table.
A teacher started it after noticing that some students felt tired during lunch. They did not want to join loud conversations every day.
At the Quiet Table, students could read, draw, or eat silently. Anyone could sit there, but they had to respect the rule: low voices only.
At first, some students thought it was strange. Later, the table became popular before big tests or after busy mornings.
The Quiet Table taught the school that not everyone rests in the same way. Some people feel better after talking. Others feel better after silence.
